title: What Nora Knew
subtitle: A Novella of Memory, Fire, and the Stories We Tell to Survive
description: Grief counselor Nora Voss has spent her career listening to the bereaved, guiding them through loss with steady hands and careful questions. Then Martin Brand walks into her office, mourning his wife in a house fire everyone calls accidental. His grief is polished, his story consistent — almost too consistent. When a diary surfaces from the dead woman's final month, small details begin to diverge from Martin's account in ways that are easy to dismiss and impossible to forget. Nora knows she should stay behind the line. But Nora has crossed a line before, with consequences she buried long ago, and the weight of that silence bends everything she hears now. As the diary pulls her deeper into a dead woman's last days, Nora must decide what she is willing to risk — and what she already suspects — before the two timelines collide in a revelation that changes everything she thought she understood about her client, his wife, and herself.

editorReview.text: What Nora Knew pulls off a genuinely rare feat: a twist that doesn't just surprise but retroactively rewrites every clue Nora chased, revealing the whole investigation as bait she was meant to swallow. The fire-aftermath scenes carry real tactile authority—'shadows still smelled of fire,' the ash pattern wrong—and Nora's slow slide from grief-counselor crusader to someone who realizes she's been wielded as a weapon is quietly devastating.
